title: Problem awareness — inside a GLP-1 gut

beats.text: This is what's happening inside your gut. A GLP-1 causes your appetite to slow down, and suddenly going to the bathroom gets harder.
beats.visual: Translucent character stops mid-bite with a sharp expression of discomfort as the interior stomach becomes visible; movement already underway in frame one. No swelling into obstruction.
beats.why: Preserve the user's exact hook. The appetite/bathroom contradiction creates immediate recognition while the anatomical view promises an explanation.

beats.text: Watch the stomach. Food moves through it with muscular contractions. A GLP-1 can slow how quickly that food leaves. See how it stays there longer instead of passing through at the same pace?
beats.visual: Side-on illustrative stomach follows food through continued contractions and a slower exit. Hold one legible action; label illustration. No precise retention time shown.
beats.why: Uses deictic language to direct attention to a changing process rather than merely naming an organ. Does not imply full gastric paralysis.

beats.text: You feel full for longer. But you still want to go to the bathroom comfortably and get on with your day.
beats.visual: New dining-room wide view: character sets plate aside, shifts uncomfortably and looks toward an interrupted daily activity. No promised post-product result.
beats.why: Make the desired change concrete before introducing the familiar remedies; no unsupported product outcome is promised.

beats.text: Now watch what happens when you reach for MiraLAX or fiber. MiraLAX holds water in your stool, helping it soften and pass. A bulking fiber like psyllium absorbs water and helps form stool. Both can help you go.
beats.visual: Direct cut on 'Now watch' to a split colon illustration: water remains with stool on the PEG side; hydrated psyllium gel forms on the other. Both processes remain functional.
beats.why: Presents what the familiar attempts actually do, so the viewer can understand a relevant distinction instead of being told the options are useless.

beats.text: What would another approach need to do differently? It would need to address the discomfort you're still feeling, so you can get on with your day.
beats.visual: Cut to the character pausing a normal daily activity; on the question show a neutral goal card: COMFORT THROUGH YOUR DAY. No ingredient imagery yet.
beats.why: Creates a criterion for considering a new approach before ingredients are introduced. The viewer is not assumed to know or accept a solution.

beats.text: Imagine finishing dinner without that tight, uncomfortable pressure in your belly. Imagine settling into bed without an overfull feeling keeping your attention on your gut.
beats.visual: Two distinct imagined scenes, both labeled as imagined: a relaxed character finishes dinner, then a new bedroom composition shows them settling into bed. Enter each scene on its own 'Imagine'; match illustration style and character identity. No Motilli pack, ingredient effects or medical before/after.
beats.why: Shows relief from discomfort as two recognizable activities. Placement before product identifies aspiration rather than claiming measured or typical product results.

beats.text: With that goal in mind, let's look at a formula built around three ingredients.
beats.visual: Direct cut after the second imagined moment to three neutral numbered ingredient areas; reveal celery only on the next beat's 'First'. No logo.
beats.why: Ingredients enter only once the viewer understands what the next option should achieve. The formula is introduced for evaluation, not declared a proven root-cause cure.

beats.text: First, there's a plant compound in celery called apigenin. In mice fed a high-fat diet, it reduced inflammatory signals in the colon and helped normalize certain muscle responses. That research doesn't show that celery makes a GLP-1 stomach empty faster.
beats.visual: Celery macro, then a clearly labeled MOUSE STUDY research diagram of the colon. Indicate lower inflammatory markers and studied contraction responses, not restored human stomach emptying. No brand or product.
beats.why: Explains a concrete observed action and its experimental context. A mouse-colon illustration cannot masquerade as the viewer's proven product response.

beats.text: Second, chlorophyllin, a derivative of the green pigment in plants. It's been studied for odor control, with mixed findings. Reducing odor isn't the same thing as removing gas or relieving constipation.
beats.visual: Distinct chlorophyllin ingredient dish, followed by separate ODOR and GAS VOLUME labels. No bubbles disappear and no bloating before/after is shown.
beats.why: Separates the endpoint investigated from the desired digestive symptom; avoids assigning an unestablished action to chlorophyllin.

beats.text: Third, prebiotic fiber. Watch a type called FOS reach the large intestine, where beneficial bacteria use it as food. That fermentation can also produce gas, so tolerance matters.
beats.visual: FOS reaches a distinct colon microenvironment and is used by resident microbes. A small gas bubble appears without pathological pressure symbolism.
beats.why: Shows the supported prebiotic action at its actual location and includes the relevant tolerance limitation.

beats.text: These ingredients can be combined in a supplement. That doesn't establish that the combination treats GLP-1 constipation.
beats.visual: Three neutral ingredient labels group together. No arrows imply a proven shared treatment outcome. Hold the qualification at readable size with narration.
beats.why: All ingredient explanation is complete before brand entry; the synthesis distinguishes a combined formula from a proven combined treatment mechanism.

beats.text: Motilli combines these three ingredients into two daily gummies. Celery, chlorophyllin and prebiotic fiber, together in one daily supplement.
beats.visual: First Motilli pack and logo reveal on 'Motilli'; two accurate gummies and ingredient callouts. No earlier branding.
beats.why: Uses the user's direct bridge after ingredient explanation; states formulation presence without asserting clinical synergy or replacing treatment.

beats.text: Take them as directed with water. If you're looking for these ingredients in one daily supplement, tap to shop Motilli, backed by a 90-day money-back guarantee.
beats.visual: Character's evening water-and-gummy routine, then product and Shop Motilli with verified guarantee. New composition; no symptomatic transformation.
beats.why: Closes on the actual offered formula and seller-listed policy. Treatment superiority or bodily outcomes are not invented to close the sale.

beats.visual: Hold package and readable CTA, music resolves.
beats.why: Three seconds to read and act; not extra efficacy messaging.

status: Revised goal-first transition and two-sentence aspirational future pacing. Complete factual copy; therapeutic UMS remains unestablished.

title: Ingredient-led — Day 1, Day 2, Day 3

beats.text: This is what happens when you take celery, chlorophyll and fiber every day when you're constipated on a GLP-1.
beats.visual: First frame: three unbranded ingredient symbols move into a simple calendar as the translucent character gestures emphatically toward DAY 1. Bright readable action, no gastric-slowdown setup or symptom cure.
beats.why: Promises the requested temporal walkthrough immediately. The calendar introduces the sequence; no competitor-remedy detour delays day one.

beats.text: Day one. You start the routine. First, there's a plant compound in celery called apigenin. Alongside it are chlorophyllin, a derivative of chlorophyll, and prebiotic fiber.
beats.visual: DAY 1 badge; distinct botanical/ingredient macro panels identify apigenin, chlorophyllin and FOS, followed by an unbranded serving beside water. No Motilli visible and no physiological improvement.
beats.why: Introduces what is being taken at the start rather than inventing immediate efficacy. Preserve the requested apigenin introduction within the timeline.

beats.stage: Day 2: continued use and FOS function
beats.text: Day two. You continue as directed. The prebiotic fiber is food for beneficial bacteria in your large intestine. As they ferment it, they can also produce gas, so pay attention to how your gut responds.
beats.visual: DAY 2 starts on a new countertop routine shot. Then clear DAY 2 marker before a distinct colon-microbe illustration labeled GENERAL PREBIOTIC FUNCTION; use particles and a small gas bubble, not a cure animation.
beats.why: Gives the second day an observable routine action and explains a supported fiber function. Clearing the day marker avoids claiming a measured day-two transit or microbiome milestone.

beats.text: Day three. Check in with your body. Are bowel movements easier? Is the pressure or discomfort changing? Those are things to notice, not results everyone gets by day three.
beats.visual: DAY 3 badge; character records a neutral symptom check-in with bowel comfort and pressure fields left unscored. No fabricated downward symptom chart, dramatic bathroom success or green check of efficacy.
beats.why: A check-in pays off the chronology without inventing a typical outcome. Questions name the viewer's desired change; neutral records preserve uncertainty.

beats.text: Imagine finishing dinner without that tight, uncomfortable pressure in your belly. Imagine settling into bed without an overfull feeling keeping your attention on your gut.
beats.visual: Remove day badge completely. Separate two-shot imagined-goal section, labeled IMAGINE: new dinner composition and new bedtime composition. No product image, study framing or time-to-relief stamp.
beats.why: Retains the user's two-sentence discomfort-focused future pacing while separating an aspiration from a documented Day 3 result.

beats.text: Motilli combines these three ingredients into two daily gummies. This combination doesn't have an established three-day constipation-relief timeline.
beats.visual: First Motilli pack and two accurate gummies on 'Motilli'; retain spoken timeline qualification as readable captions. No anatomical transformation.
beats.why: Keeps the user's exact bridge after the walkthrough and makes the product's limits explicit instead of using a misleading day-specific promise.

beats.text: If you're looking for these ingredients in one daily supplement, tap to shop Motilli, backed by a 90-day money-back guarantee.
beats.visual: Distinct front-facing product/Shop Motilli offer card; no countdown or fabricated review/customer count.
beats.why: Connects the known formula and actual offer to a concrete next action without implying proven three-day treatment efficacy.

beats.visual: Hold product and CTA for three seconds; quiet music resolves.
beats.why: Provides readable decision time at the close.

status: Direct daily routine walkthrough. Days do not establish clinical response or ingredient-action timing; A/B unchanged.
